steps.title: Make Ringers solution (500 mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 11.6 mL 5 M NaCl, 5.8 mL 250 mM KCl, 5 mL 1 M CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 2.5 mL 1 M HEPES (pH 7.2); adjust pH to 7.2 with NaOH, add water to a final volume of 500 mL and store at 4 °C for up to three months.

steps.title: Prepare MS‑222/Tricaine solution (400 mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 400 mg MS‑222/Tricaine to obtain 15.3 mM, add 2.1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 9.0) to reach 5.25 mM, adjust pH to 7.2 with NaOH, bring the volume to 400 mL, and store at 4 °C for up to three months.

steps.title: Make MS‑222 working solution (≤100 mL)
steps.instruction: Mix 4.2 mL of the MS‑222/Tricaine solution with Ringers solution and bring the total volume to 100 mL (final 15.3 mM MS‑222).

steps.title: Prepare cold protease stock (100 mg/mL)
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL 1× PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) to 100 mg protease from B. licheniformis, pipette repeatedly to dissolve, bring volume to 1 mL with PBS, aliquot 100 mL into cryotubes and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare DNase I stock (20 U/µL)
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL 1× PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) to 10 mg DNase I, pipette repeatedly to dissolve, bring volume to 1 mL with PBS, aliquot 100 mL into microcentrifuge tubes and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Make cold protease working solution (10 mg/mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 100 µL cold protease stock (100 mg/mL), 5 µL 1 M CaCl₂ (final 5 mM), 1 µL 0.5 M EDTA (final 0.5 mM), 5 µL DNase stock (100 U/mL), and add DPBS to a final volume of 1 mL; mix by pipetting and keep on ice (4 °C) until use.

steps.title: Prepare DPBS‑BSA solution (0.01 % BSA)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.5 mg BSA in 4.5 mL 1× DPBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺), bring volume to 5 mL, keep on ice (4 °C) until use.

steps.title: Create silicone polymer plates
steps.instruction: Mix 40 mL SYLGARD 184 silicone elastomer base (91 %) with 4 mL curing agent (9 %) by inversion on a nutator; store upright at –20 °C for at least 24 h to let bubbles rise, then pour into 60 × 15 mm Petri dishes to the desired height, incubate at 37 °C for ≥12 h to set, and store plates at room temperature until needed.

steps.title: Dissect zebrafish heads
steps.instruction: Perform head isolation using two 21 G needles attached to 1 mL syringes on an ice‑cold silicone plate containing MS‑222 working solution.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 zebrafish embryos (72 h post‑fertilization) to the silicone plate with MS‑222 working solution on an ice bath.
Attach two 1 mL insulin syringes (plungers removed) to 21 G needles.
Place the needles at a 45° angle dorsal and ventral to each embryo’s head, just posterior to the pectoral fin, with the sharper edge facing the silicone surface.
Simultaneously drag the needles across the embryo in a scissor‑like motion to sever the head from the trunk.

steps.title: Dissociate heads with cold protease
steps.instruction: Enzymatically dissociate the isolated heads in cold protease working solution on ice.

substeps.instruction: Transfer each head to a well of a 24‑well ultra‑low attachment plate.
Aspirate the Ringer’s solution and add 1 mL cold protease working solution.
Gently aspirate and expel the contents into a 1 mL pipette tip twice, then place the plate on an ice bath.
Triturate with a 1 mL tip for 15 s, then repeat aspiration/expulsion every 2 min.
Continue trituration until the tissue is fully dissociated (≈25 min for 72 hpf heads), monitoring under a dissecting microscope.

steps.title: Generate single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Filter, wash, and centrifuge the dissociation mixture to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Position a 40 µm cell strainer over a 15 mL tube on an ice bath.
Pour the dissociation mixture through the strainer; tap the strainer gently to release undissociated clumps.
Add 9 mL ice‑cold 1× DPBS through the strainer to wash, dilute, and stop protease activity.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 600 × g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ice‑cold DPBS‑BSA by trituration with a 1 mL tip.

steps.title: Assess cell viability with trypan blue
steps.instruction: Determine cell viability using trypan blue exclusion on ice.

substeps.instruction: Mix 2 µL 0.4 % trypan blue with 2 µL of the cell suspension.
Incubate the mixture on an ice bath for 2 min.
Transfer 2 µL of the mixture onto a glass slide, place a coverslip over it, and view under a compound microscope.
Confirm viability by the absence of trypan blue staining; viable cells can then be used for downstream applications such as FACS or RNA‑seq.

description: Validation of protocol Differential tendon gene expression in cranial tenocytes dissociated with cold vs. warm protease We first examined expression differences in hallmark marker genes crucial for proper tendon development and maturation by performing pseudo-bulk differential expression analysis, whereby all cells were integrated, clustered by condition (e.g., cold or warm dissociation), and the conditions compared against each other. Comparison of warm and cold conditions found a significant loss in expression of scxa, mkxa, tnmd, thbs4b , and sox9a with warm dissociation ( Figure 3 ), while the zinc-finger transcription factor egr1 was upregulated with warm dissociation ( Figure 3 ). We also noticed significant upregulation of TGFβ signal transduction genes such as smad3a, tgif1 , and tgfb1a in the warm condition ( Figure 4A , Figure 5A ), suggesting that cells enter a stressed, TGFβ-dependent pro-inflammatory/pro-fibrotic state. Figure 3. Differential expression of tenocyte marker genes between warm vs. cold dissociation conditions. Violin plots of tenocyte marker genes scxa, mkxa, tnmd, thbs4b , and sox9a all show significant downregulation, whereas egr1 displays upregulation in warm dissociation conditions. Collagenase dissociation at warm temperatures elevates stress responses in embryonic tenocytes To try and define specific vs. general effects of warm collagenase dissociation on the tenocyte transcriptome, we identified genes either upregulated or downregulated in warm vs. cold conditions using pseudo-bulk differential expression analysis and compared the results with similar studies in other cell types. Overall, 716 genes were upregulated in warm conditions and 2,142 were upregulated in cold conditions with adjusted p-values 0.5 or < -0.5 with adjusted p-value < 0.05.
